items.title: Witkoff says U.S. demands any Iran nuclear deal last indefinitely

featured_image.name: Steve Witkoff says Iran nuclear agreement hinges on weapon verification | The Jerusalem Post

items.description:
U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff told a private gathering of AIPAC donors in Washington on Tuesday that the Trump administration is insisting any nuclear deal with Iran include no sunset clause, according to a report by Axios citing a U.S. official and two other people familiar with his remarks.[1]

"We go to the Iranians with the understanding that there will be no sunset provision," Witkoff said, according to Axios. "Regardless of whether a deal is achieved, our position is clear: you must adhere to these terms for life."[1]

The demand, made just two days before the next round of U.S.-Iran talks scheduled for Thursday in Geneva, marks a direct attempt to address what President Trump and other critics have long called the central flaw of the 2015 nuclear agreement brokered by the Obama administration. Under that deal, known as the JCPOA, most restrictions on Iran's nuclear activities were set to expire between eight and 25 years after signing.[2][3][1]

items.title: Zimbabwe halts all raw mineral and lithium exports

featured_image.name: Zimbabwe Suspends Exports of Lithium Concentrates, Raw ...

items.description:
Zimbabwe on Wednesday suspended exports of all raw minerals and lithium concentrates with immediate effect, a sweeping move that tightens state control over resources critical to global clean-energy supply chains and accelerates the southern African nation's push for domestic processing.[1][2]

Mines and Mining Development Minister Polite Kambamura announced the ban at a press conference in Harare, stating that the suspension applies to all minerals currently in transit and will remain in place until further notice. "Government expects cooperation of the mining industry on this measure which has been taken in the national interest," Kambamura said, according to the ministry's official statement.[3][2]

items.title: Canada sends $8M in food aid to Cuba amid U.S. fuel blockade

featured_image.name: Mexico sends shipment of humanitarian aid to Cuba : Peoples ...

items.description:
Canada announced on Wednesday it will provide $8 million Canadian (approximately US$6.7 million) in food assistance to Cuba, as Mexico dispatched a second shipment of humanitarian supplies to the island, where an intensifying U.S. fuel blockade has triggered what the United Nations has called a looming "humanitarian collapse."[1][2]

The twin announcements mark a growing international response to Cuba's deepening crisis, which has left millions of people facing prolonged blackouts, dwindling food supplies, and the near-total collapse of transportation on the Caribbean island of 11 million.

items.title: Uber unveils air taxi booking with Joby in Dubai

featured_image.name: Joby Aviation flying taxi launching service in Dubai UAE in 2026

items.description:
Uber Technologies and Joby Aviation on Wednesday unveiled "Uber Air powered by Joby," giving riders a first look at how they will be able to book an all-electric air taxi directly through the Uber app. Joby expects to carry its first passengers later this year in Dubai, where it holds a six-year exclusive agreement with the emirate's Roads and Transport Authority to operate air taxi services.[1][2]

The announcement marks one of the most concrete steps yet in the long-running effort to bring electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft into mainstream urban transportation.

items.title: Modi arrives in Israel for historic state visit

featured_image.name: Narendra Modi becomes first Indian PM to visit Israel

items.description:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in Israel on February 25 for a two-day state visit, greeted on the tarmac at Ben Gurion Airport by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a scene that echoed their first encounter during Modi's landmark 2017 trip. The visit, Modi's second to Israel and his first since beginning a third term in office, comes at a moment of heightened volatility in the region, as the United States escalates its military posture toward Iran and diplomatic efforts over Tehran's nuclear program remain unresolved.[1][2][3][4]

The trip is designed to deepen cooperation in defense, artificial intelligence, quantum computing, and cybersecurity, with a series of bilateral agreements expected to be signed on February 26. But it also places India at the center of a broader geopolitical contest, as Netanyahu seeks to draw New Delhi into a proposed alliance of nations aimed at confronting what he called "radical axes" in the Middle East.[2][5][6]

items.title: Trump demands Iran renounce nuclear weapons ahead of Geneva talks Thursday

items.description: The United States and Iran are set to meet Thursday in Geneva for a third round of indirect nuclear negotiations, talks that U.S. officials have described as perhaps the last chance for a diplomatic resolution before Washington turns to military force. The meeting comes as President Trump, in his State of the Union address Tuesday evening, declared he would "never allow the world's number one sponsor of terror" to possess a nuclear weapon.[1][2]

items.title: China says it met Phase One trade deal terms, warns US against new tariffs

featured_image.name: China’s leverage rises before high-stakes summit as Supreme Court curbs Trump tariffs

items.description:
China's Commerce Ministry on Tuesday asserted that Beijing has fulfilled its obligations under the 2020 Phase One trade agreement and urged Washington not to use an ongoing Section 301 investigation as a pretext for imposing new tariffs. The statement adds a layer of tension to the bilateral relationship just weeks before President Donald Trump is scheduled to visit Beijing from March 31 to April 2.[1][2][3]

A ministry spokesperson said China had "upheld the spirit of the contract" despite pandemic-related disruptions and "faithfully fulfilled" its commitments on intellectual property protections, financial and agricultural market openings, and trade cooperation. The spokesperson warned the United States to "view the Phase One agreement's implementation objectively and rationally," adding that Washington "should not shift blame" and "must not exploit opportunities to create problems".[1]

items.title: Largest-ever ALMA image reveals Milky Way's hidden core

featured_image.name: ALMA reveals Milky Way's core in largest-ever mosaic ...

items.description:
Astronomers have unveiled the largest image ever captured by the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), revealing the swirling splendor of cold, star-forming gases at the center of the Milky Way in unprecedented detail. The mosaic, released Wednesday by the European Southern Observatory, spans more than 650 light-years and covers the dense clouds of gas and dust surrounding the supermassive black hole at the galaxy's core.[1][2]

The image is the centerpiece of a major new dataset from ACES — the ALMA Central Molecular Zone Exploration Survey — a collaboration involving more than 160 scientists at over 70 institutions worldwide. The findings are detailed in five papers accepted for publication in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, with a sixth under final review.[3][1]
